hlv.plain: What your future earnings are worth today, after your own spending, until you retire.

annuityFactor.plain: How many years of a yearly amount a lump sum must cover, after allowing for prices rising and money earning a return.

annuityDue.plain: The first year's money is needed straight away, not at the end of the year.

realRate.plain: The return on savings after taking out price rises (or income growth).

surrenderValue.plain: What you get back if you stop a savings policy early. Usually much less than you paid in the first years.

gsv.plain: The minimum the insurer must pay back, set as a percentage of the premiums you have paid.

ssv.plain: A value the insurer may offer instead, if it is higher than the guaranteed value.

paidUp.plain: You stop paying, but the policy carries on with a smaller amount, in proportion to what you have paid.

maturity.plain: What a savings policy pays if you live to the end of it. It does not protect your family if you die.

deathCover.plain: What your family gets if you die while the policy is running. Only this counts in your gap.

discontinuance.plain: If you stop a ULIP in the first 5 years, your money is moved here and paid out only after the lock-in ends.

lockIn.plain: The years during which you can't take your money out.

rider.plain: An optional add-on to a policy, for an extra premium.

insurerLimit.plain: The most cover an insurer will usually offer, set as a multiple of your income. Ours is a placeholder.

term.plain: Pays your family if you die during the policy term. Nothing is paid back if you live, which is why it costs the least.

endowment.plain: A savings plan with a small amount of life cover, paying a lump sum on a fixed date.

wholeLife.plain: Cover that lasts for your whole life (to a set age such as 99 or 100).

ulip.plain: A unit-linked plan: most of your money is invested in market funds, with some life cover.
